This is a formal escalation. We have two independent issues: blank VAT totals since 2.1.0, and SSO login failing for finance since the identity migration. The VAT fix was promised for Sep 20 and the SSO fix for Sep 26. Both dates passed without a working fix, our chases on 22 and 23 September went unanswered, and we still have no explanation or dates. Please explain what happened on each issue and when each will actually be fixed.

Dana Okafor, Finance Lead, Contoso

claims.text: The blank VAT totals root cause is the BILLING-V2 refactor, which moved VAT rounding to integer math in 2.1.0, dropping fractional cents and blanking the export totals — a change recorded as still unreviewed (ORB-150, raised 10 Sep).
claims.quote: The BILLING-V2 refactor moved VAT rounding to integer math in 2.1.0, which drops fractional cents and blanks the export totals. That change is still unreviewed.

claims.text: A separate VAT rounding regression ticket, ORB-150 'BILLING-V2: VAT rounding regression', was created on 10 Sep, confirming the defect was known on the build line rather than being client-side configuration.
claims.quote: Issue created: BILLING-V2: VAT rounding regression

claims.text: ORB-101 was resolved on 21 Sep on the claim that the VAT fix was in 2.1.3 and totals were verified internally, but the fix was not effective: the ticket was reopened on 26 Sep because the finance sandbox still showed blank VAT totals on 2.1.3.
claims.quote: Resolved in 2.1.3; totals verified on our side.

claims.text: Version 2.1.3 did not carry a working VAT fix — the finance sandbox still showed blank VAT totals on 2.1.3, so the Sep 20 release line (2.1.3) did not resolve the issue.
claims.quote: Reopened: the finance sandbox still shows blank VAT totals on 2.1.3.

claims.text: The VAT issue was only actually fixed in 2.1.4, when the VAT rounding path was corrected and exports verified with finance; ORB-101 was then re-resolved on 28 Sep.
claims.quote: Fixed in 2.1.4. The VAT rounding path was corrected; exports verified with finance.

claims.text: The blank VAT totals originated in the 2.1.0 upgrade and were still present on 2.1.3; the actual correction was the VAT rounding path fixed in 2.1.4, verified with finance on Sep 28.
claims.quote: Fixed in 2.1.4. The VAT rounding path was corrected; exports verified with finance.

claims.text: Ravi Menon closed ORB-101 as resolved on Sep 21 claiming the VAT fix was in 2.1.3, but that claim was wrong — the finance sandbox still showed blank VAT totals on 2.1.3, which led to a reopen by Maya Rao on Sep 26.
claims.quote: Reopened: the finance sandbox still shows blank VAT totals on 2.1.3.

skepticNotes.text: Claim 35 states Ravi Menon 'gave Contoso' the fix dates on Sep 30, but the cited event e_783c4feb1b9b86e1 is a Slack message in the 'general' channel, not a communication to Contoso. Nothing in the record shows the escalation (e_074f5e7d4f3c7d86/e_bba117f3af21cc47) was ever answered to the client.

Claim 4 (and 9, 26) asserts exports were 'verified with finance' in 2.1.4 on Sep 28, but Dana Okafor's Sep 28 email (e_58b4307b8f195cf4) says VAT totals are still blank, and the Sep 29 escalation (e_1ece4b255c3205b3) says 'VAT still blank.' The client-side verification at Sep 28 is contradicted by the client's own reports.

Claim 16 (verified with Contoso finance, closing, Sep 30) is contradicted: nothing from Contoso confirms SSO worked, and the last client statement (Sep 29, e_1ece4b255c3205b3) was 'SSO still down.' The jira transition e_c3a6ca3911af61e4 records 'Resolved → Resolved' with no intervening rejection/reopen from Dana's Sep 27 'still failing' report.

Claim 0 says the BILLING-V2 integer-math rounding change 'blanks the export totals,' but the cited item e_55f39a25a1a6af43 also states the change is 'still unreviewed,' i.e. not confirmed as the production cause. The causal leap from an unreviewed code change to the observed blanking is asserted, not evidenced; no deploy/rollback record links 2.1.0's shipping to this change.

Claim 2 says ORB-101 'was resolved on 21 Sep on the claim that the VAT fix was in 2.1.3 and totals verified internally,' but the citation e_29b5f45b5a41b9c7 supports only 'totals verified on our side.' There is no record showing 2.1.3 was actually deployed/built containing the fix; the claim assumes 2.1.3 existed with a fix, which the reopen proves false but the res-outcome is inferred.

Long gap in the record between Sep 21 ORB-101 resolution and Sep 22-23 client chases with no Orbit reply, and again Sep 26 reopen to Sep 28: the internal Slack (orbit-support) shows no investigation activity on ORB-101 between the Sep 24 root-cause note (e_55f39a25a1a6af43) and the Sep 28 close, leaving the actual fix decision undocumented.

Claims 20/21/27/28 assert the Sep 22-23 chases 'went unanswered,' but the searches show email threads were retrieved (e_e6da783262af7a16, e_58b4307b8f195cf4); the finding of 'no reply' should be grounded in the full thread contents, which are not quoted. It is an inference from absence rather than a documented nil-response, and no internal Slack/email record of Orbit discussing the chases is cited.

Claim 15 says Leo Park resolved ORB-140 'on the sole basis that the identity migration was complete'; but the ORB-160 record (e_9c1b485fd52fb5ac, e_e3d40dc0edf3ee19) shows the SAML certificate defect was known internally as of Sep 20/29. The draft treats the SSO root cause as only discovered Sep 29 by Sam Ortiz (claim 14), yet ORB-160 was created Sep 20 — the causation timeline is internally inconsistent.

ORB-150 (created Sep 10) is cited as evidence the VAT defect was 'known on the build line,' but no record shows it was ever linked to ORB-101, prioritized, or scheduled. The question of why a known regression in the same module did not inform the Sep 21 resolution is left unanswered.

ORB-160 (SAML certificate dropped) is referenced but never appears as a resolution source for ORB-140 in the draft claims except via Sam Ortiz's Sep 29 comment. Whether ORB-140 was actually closed against 3.4.1 (or prematurely) before 3.4.1 shipped is unanswered; no deployment record for 3.4.1 exists in the registry.

Claim 31 asserts responsibility 'passed to Maya Rao on Sep 26-28,' but the records only show Maya reopened and commented; there is no handoff/assignment change event. Ownership transfer is inferred from actions, not documented.

No deployment/release records (CI, release notes, changelog) were searched or found for 2.1.3, 2.1.4, or 3.4.1, despite search_slack('deploy') being run. Whether 2.1.4 or 3.4.1 actually shipped before being declared fixed is unverified — a never-satisfied angle.

The Sep 30 formal escalation (e_074f5e7d4f3c7d86/e_bba117f3af21cc47) duplicated under two ids suggests an email thread was fetched; yet no Orbit email reply to it appears in the record. The only response is Ravi's general-channel Slack. Whether Contoso received any written explanation is unaddressed.
